references.text: The Israelites set out from the Desert of Sinai, and the cloud stopped in the Desert of Paran. This describes the same departure from the Desert of Sinai.
The place was called Kibroth-hattaavah (graves of craving) because there they buried the people who had shown craving. This explains the origin of the place name mentioned in the verse.
The people began to complain and crave meat at Kibroth-hattaavah, which led to the place receiving its name.
Moses reminds the people of the events at Kibroth-hattaavah where they aroused the Lord's anger.
The Israelites came to the Desert of Sinai and camped there. This is the place from which they now set out.
